title: Becoming an Experience Creator
lead: Order taker or experience creator: the four pillars, a real turnaround, and three boxes to tick every day.

and advocacy: what an experience creator earns.

read.where: The difference between **compliance** and **connection** defines our brand. **The Order Taker** focuses on the **transaction**: they listen to the request, process it accurately and say goodbye. The interaction is **forgettable**. **The Experience Creator** focuses on the **interaction**: they read the customer’s energy, uncover **hidden needs** and leave a **lasting positive impression**.

keyPoints.line: means they want speed and peace of mind.
means they want guidance and reassurance.
warm, human words instead of robotic ones.

read.bigIdea: Read between the lines. Then speak like a person.
read.where: The first two of the **four pillars of experience creation**.

stops.name: Active observation
stops.text: Look for **emotional cues**: body language, tone of voice, context clues. Then identify the **why**. If a customer is in a rush, they don’t just want a product; they want **speed and peace of mind**. If they are indecisive, they want **guidance and reassurance**.

stops.name: Elevated language
stops.text: Replace transactional scripts with **warm, human responses**.

offer what you know before they ask.

apologize for the frustration, then fix it.

read.bigIdea: Solve the next problem. Own the vibe.
read.where: The other two pillars of experience creation.

stops.name: Anticipatory service
stops.text: Think **one step ahead** of the customer, and provide the **unasked extra**. If they buy a bottle of wine, don’t wait for them to ask about it: offer information you know about the product.

stops.name: Emotional ownership
stops.text: You cannot control a customer’s bad day, but you **entirely control** how they feel when they’re interacting with you. **Own mistakes instantly**: if something goes wrong, apologize for the frustration caused and focus **immediately on the solution**.

sections.name: A turnaround and the daily checklist

keyPoints.line: use their name naturally, at least twice.
one extra they didn’t ask for.
a human moment that isn’t about the sale.
check with the kitchen or bar: see what we can do.

read.bigIdea: Three boxes to tick, every single day.
read.where: To keep this mindset alive, challenge yourself to tick these **three boxes every single day**.

stops.name: The Name Drop
stops.text: Use the customer’s **name** naturally **at least twice** during the conversation.

stops.name: The Plus-One
stops.text: Give **one extra** piece of advice, validation or assistance that the customer **didn’t explicitly ask for**.

stops.name: The Personal Touch
stops.text: Share a moment of **genuine human connection** (a laugh, a shared compliment or active empathy) that has **nothing to do with the transaction** itself.

cards.q: An Order Taker’s primary goal is to…
What does an Experience Creator leave the customer with?
cards.answer: Loyalty and advocacy: an emotional high

cards.q: How does an Experience Creator solve problems?
wrong: Waits for the guest to suggest one

cards.q: A customer is in a rush. Beyond the product, what do they want?
Instead of “Is that all?”, an experience creator says…
cards.answer: “What else can I help you take care of today?”

cards.q: Instead of “I don’t know, not my department,” you say…
cards.answer: “Let’s find out. I’ll connect you with the right person.”

cards.q: A guest buys a bottle of wine. What does anticipatory service look like?
cards.answer: Offer what you know about it without waiting to be asked
wrong: Wait for them to ask questions
Recommend a second bottle right away

cards.q: Something goes wrong at the table. Emotional ownership means…
cards.answer: Apologize for the frustration caused and focus on the solution
How the customer feels when they’re with you

cards.q: Which of these is not one of the four pillars?
The Name Drop: how often do you use the customer’s name?
cards.answer: Naturally, at least twice in the conversation
wrong: Every time you speak to them

cards.answer: One extra piece of advice, validation or help they didn’t ask for
wrong: Adding one more item to their order

cards.q: A guest asks for something that’s sold out. The experience creator…
cards.answer: Says it’s popular and sold out, then offers to check with the kitchen or bar
wrong: Says “We’re out of that right now. Sorry.”
Suggests they come back another day
Tells them to pick something else

cards.q: The Personal Touch is a moment of connection that…
cards.answer: Has nothing to do with the transaction itself
wrong: Comes after the check is paid
